subject: Physics
topic: Motion in a Plane: Projectiles, Relative Frames & Curvilinear Motion
title: Grade 9 Olympiad Physics Core 1A Ontology: Motion in a Plane (Projectiles, Relative Frames & Curvilinear Motion)

stage_1_choose.name: Orthogonal Frame & Origin Declaration
stage_1_choose.action: Declare mutually perpendicular spatial axes (x, y), reference directions (+x horizontal, +y vertical), and clock zero t = 0.
stage_1_choose.invariant: Physical trajectory geometry is invariant under spatial coordinate translation and rotation.

stage_2_represent.name: Decoupled Vector & Relative State Representation
stage_2_represent.action: Decompose vectors into orthogonal components (u_x = u cos theta, u_y = u sin theta) or construct Galilean relative velocity triangles (v_A/B = v_A - v_B).
stage_2_represent.invariant: Orthogonal independence: horizontal kinematics and vertical kinematics decouple completely and share only clock time t.

stage_3_connect.name: Trajectory Quad & Curvature Invariants
stage_3_connect.action: Select the governing 2D equations: Cartesian parabola y(x) = x tan theta - g*x^2 / (2*u^2*cos^2 theta), or Frenet-Serret decomposition a = a_t u_t + a_n u_n.
stage_3_connect.invariant: Under uniform gravity, horizontal acceleration is zero (a_x = 0) and vertical acceleration is strictly constant (a_y = -g).

stage_4_execute_and_check.name: Algebraic Execution & Limiting Boundary Verification
stage_4_execute_and_check.action: Solve closed-form algebraic expressions; verify asymptotic limits (theta -> 0 deg, 90 deg, 45 deg, g -> 0, v_rel collinear) and base SI dimensional homogeneity.
stage_4_execute_and_check.invariant: All range/height formulas must have dimension [L]; velocities [L T^-1]; accelerations [L T^-2]; angles dimensionless [1].

structural_pillars.name: Orthogonal Component Independence
structural_pillars.principle: Perpendicular motions are completely independent and decouple into two separate 1D kinematic systems linked solely by shared clock t.

structural_pillars.name: Galilean Relative Frame Transformation
structural_pillars.principle: Velocity transforms via vector subtraction v_A/B = v_A - v_B. Under identical gravity, relative acceleration vanishes identically (a_rel = 0).
structural_pillars.canonical_expression: v_AB = v_A - v_B; a_rel = a_A - a_B = (-g) - (-g) = 0

structural_pillars.name: Parabolic Geometry & Trajectory Envelopes
structural_pillars.principle: Eliminating time yields a Cartesian parabola. Level-ground range satisfies complementary angle degeneracy theta <-> 90 deg - theta.
structural_pillars.canonical_expression: y(x) = x tan theta - (g x^2) / (2 u^2 cos^2 theta); R = (u^2 sin 2theta) / g

structural_pillars.name: Normal vs Tangential Acceleration Duality
structural_pillars.principle: Total acceleration resolves into a tangential component altering speed magnitude and a normal component altering direction of motion.
structural_pillars.canonical_expression: a_t = dv/dt; a_n = v^2 / rho; |a| = sqrt(a_t^2 + a_n^2)

structural_pillars.name: Minimum Time vs Minimum Drift Extremization
structural_pillars.principle: In river crossing, time minimization requires maximizing velocity component perpendicular to banks; drift minimization requires canceling downstream current.
structural_pillars.canonical_expression: t_min = W / v_b (head straight across); sin alpha = v_r / v_b (zero drift for v_b > v_r)

PLANE-01.title: 2D Position & Velocity Component Independence
PLANE-01.definition: Decomposition of 2D position and velocity vectors into mutually independent orthogonal Cartesian components.
canonical_rules: Position vector r(t) = x(t) i + y(t) j.
Velocity vector v(t) = v_x(t) i + v_y(t) j = (dx/dt) i + (dy/dt) j.
Perpendicular motions decouple completely; changes in x have zero effect on y-motion.
operational_heuristics: Resolve all initial velocities into u_x = u cos theta and u_y = u sin theta immediately.
Never mix horizontal and vertical quantities in a single 1D equation.
boundary_conditions: theta = 0 deg: pure horizontal motion u_x = u, u_y = 0.
theta = 90 deg: pure vertical motion u_x = 0, u_y = u.

PLANE-02.title: Constant-Acceleration Equations in Vector Form
PLANE-02.definition: Vector extension of the kinematic quad under uniform 2D acceleration.
canonical_rules: v(t) = u + at.
Delta r(t) = ut + 0.5*a*t^2.
v^2 = u^2 + 2 a . Delta r (scalar product form).
operational_heuristics: Solve vector components independently along i and j.
Equate components to find collision or landing times.
boundary_conditions: a = 0: recovers 2D uniform straight-line motion Delta r = ut.
a_x = 0, a_y = -g: standard projectile equations recovered.

PLANE-03.title: Horizontal Launch from Elevated Height
PLANE-03.definition: Kinematics of a projectile launched horizontally from height h with initial velocity u i.
canonical_rules: Initial vertical velocity is identically zero: u_y = 0.
Vertical fall time is strictly t_fall = sqrt(2h / g), identical to dropping from rest.
Horizontal range is x = u * sqrt(2h / g).
Impact speed is v_impact = sqrt(u^2 + 2gh).
operational_heuristics: Find flight time from vertical drop first, then substitute into horizontal range.
Horizontal launch speed has zero effect on the time to hit the ground.
boundary_conditions: h -> 0: t_fall -> 0, range -> 0.
u -> 0: recovers pure vertical free fall from height h.

PLANE-04.title: Ground-to-Ground Oblique Projectile Flight Time & Apex
PLANE-04.definition: Kinematic landmarks of an oblique projectile: apex turnaround, summit height, and symmetric flight time.
canonical_rules: At apex summit, vertical velocity vanishes (v_y = 0) while horizontal speed remains v_x = u cos theta.
Time to apex: t_apex = (u sin theta) / g.
Total flight time on level ground: T = 2 * t_apex = (2u sin theta) / g.
Maximum apex height: H_max = (u^2 sin^2 theta) / (2g).
operational_heuristics: Remember that speed at the apex is NOT zero; it is u cos theta.
Ascent time equals descent time on level ground.
boundary_conditions: theta = 90 deg: pure vertical toss, T = 2u/g, H = u^2/(2g).
theta = 0 deg: zero height, zero flight time on level ground.

PLANE-05.title: Horizontal Range & Maximum Range Invariant
PLANE-05.definition: Formulation of horizontal range on level ground and extremization of launch angle.
canonical_rules: Horizontal range: R = u_x * T = (u^2 sin 2theta) / g.
Maximum range occurs at theta = 45 deg: R_max = u^2 / g.
At theta = 45 deg, maximum height is exactly one quarter of range: H_max = R_max / 4.
operational_heuristics: Apply R = (u^2 sin 2theta)/g ONLY when launch and landing elevations are equal.
For non-level landing, solve y(t) = h_landing for time t.
boundary_conditions: theta = 45 deg: R = R_max = u^2 / g.
theta = 0 deg or 90 deg: R = 0.

PLANE-06.title: Complementary Launch Angles & Trajectory Envelopes
PLANE-06.definition: Degeneracy of horizontal range for complementary launch angles (theta and 90 deg - theta) at equal launch speeds.
canonical_rules: Angles theta_1 and theta_2 = 90 deg - theta_1 yield identical horizontal range R.
Ratio of flight times: T_1 / T_2 = tan theta_1.
Ratio of maximum heights: H_1 / H_2 = tan^2 theta_1.
Geometric mean height relation: sqrt(H_1 * H_2) = R / 4.
Flight time product relation: T_1 * T_2 = 2R / g.
operational_heuristics: The steep trajectory has longer flight time and greater height; the flat trajectory has shorter flight time.
Use sin(2*(90 deg - theta)) = sin(180 deg - 2*theta) = sin 2theta.
boundary_conditions: theta = 45 deg: self-complementary unique maximum range.
theta -> 0 deg: flat trajectory with T -> 0, H -> 0.

PLANE-07.title: Cartesian Trajectory Parabola Equation
PLANE-07.definition: Spatial path equation y(x) obtained by eliminating time t between horizontal and vertical motions.
canonical_rules: Cartesian trajectory equation: y(x) = x tan theta - (g x^2) / (2 u^2 cos^2 theta).
Factored range form: y(x) = x tan theta * (1 - x / R).
Path is a concave-down parabola with vertex at (R/2, H_max).
operational_heuristics: Use the factored range form when horizontal range R is known to find height at any x instantly.
To hit a target at (x, y), solve the quadratic in tan theta: (g x^2 / 2u^2)*(1 + tan^2 theta) - x tan theta + y = 0.
boundary_conditions: x = 0: y = 0 (launch).
x = R: y = 0 (landing).
x = R/2: y = H_max = (R/4) * tan theta.

PLANE-08.title: Relative Velocity: River-Boat Shortest Time vs Zero Drift
PLANE-08.definition: Galilean velocity addition applied to navigation in moving fluid media.
canonical_rules: Resultant velocity relative to ground: v_ground = v_boat/water + v_water.
Shortest crossing time: steer perpendicular to banks (theta = 90 deg); t_min = W / v_b; downstream drift x = v_r * t_min.
Zero drift condition (v_b > v_r): steer upstream at sin alpha = v_r / v_b; effective crossing speed v_eff = sqrt(v_b^2 - v_r^2); time t = W / sqrt(v_b^2 - v_r^2).
Minimum drift condition when v_b < v_r: steer at cos theta = v_b / v_r; minimum drift x_min = W * sqrt((v_r/v_b)^2 - 1).
operational_heuristics: Crossing time depends strictly on the perpendicular velocity component v_y; current speed v_r cannot assist or hinder crossing time when heading perpendicular.
If engine speed is less than river speed (v_b < v_r), zero drift is physically impossible.
boundary_conditions: v_r = 0 (still water): t = W/v_b, zero drift.
v_b = v_r: zero drift angle alpha = 90 deg (heads directly upstream, stationary relative to ground).

PLANE-09.title: Relative Velocity: Rain-Man & Aircraft Wind Drift
PLANE-09.definition: Relative frame transformation for observers moving through precipitation or wind currents.
canonical_rules: Relative velocity of rain seen by moving observer: v_rain/man = v_rain - v_man.
For vertical rain v_rain = -v_r j and observer moving at v_m i: v_rel = -v_m i - v_r j.
Umbrella tilt angle from vertical: tan theta = v_man / v_rain (tilted forward in the direction of motion).
operational_heuristics: Draw vector subtraction: -v_man points backward; adding to downward rain tilts resultant forward.
Increasing running speed requires tilting the umbrella further forward.
boundary_conditions: v_man = 0: tan theta = 0 (hold umbrella vertically).
v_man -> infinity: theta -> 90 deg (hold umbrella horizontally).

PLANE-10.title: Uniform Circular Motion: Centripetal Acceleration Invariant
PLANE-10.definition: Kinematics of circular motion at constant speed, governed by continuous velocity vector rotation.
canonical_rules: Scalar speed v is constant, but velocity direction continuously changes.
Centripetal acceleration is strictly directed toward circle center: a_c = v^2 / R = omega^2 * R.
Period T = 2*pi*R / v = 2*pi / omega; frequency f = 1/T.
Velocity vector and acceleration vector are mutually perpendicular at all times (v . a_c = 0).
operational_heuristics: Because v . a = 0, rate of change of speed is zero (dv/dt = 0); all acceleration is purely normal.
Do not confuse uniform circular motion with zero acceleration.
boundary_conditions: R -> infinity: a_c -> 0 (straight-line uniform motion).
omega -> 0: static rest.

PLANE-11.title: Non-Uniform Curvilinear Motion: Tangential vs Normal Components
PLANE-11.definition: General planar curvilinear kinematics decomposed into intrinsic Frenet-Serret coordinates.
canonical_rules: Total acceleration vector: a = a_t u_t + a_n u_n.
Tangential component alters speed magnitude: a_t = dv/dt = (v . a) / v.
Normal component alters velocity direction: a_n = v^2 / rho = sqrt(|a|^2 - a_t^2).
Radius of curvature of trajectory: rho = v^2 / a_n = v^3 / |v x a|.
operational_heuristics: At projectile apex: velocity is horizontal u_x = u cos theta, acceleration is vertical g => a_t = 0 and a_n = g => rho_apex = (u^2 cos^2 theta) / g.
Speed is increasing when a_t > 0; decreasing when a_t < 0; instantaneous extremum when a_t = 0.
boundary_conditions: Straight line: rho -> infinity => a_n = 0, a = a_t.
Circle: rho = R => a_n = v^2/R.

first_move_atlas.cue: 2D position vector r(t) or velocity v(t) with orthogonal (x, y) coordinates
first_move_atlas.representation: Orthogonal Cartesian coordinate frame (x, y) with independent 1D projections
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Decompose motion into independent perpendicular components: r(t) = x(t) i + y(t) j and v(t) = v_x(t) i + v_y(t) j, linked solely by clock t
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Mixing horizontal and vertical kinematic variables inside a single 1D equation

first_move_atlas.cue: Constant acceleration in 2D with vector quantities u and a
first_move_atlas.representation: Vector UVATS table separating horizontal (i) and vertical (j) components
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Apply 2D vector kinematic quad equations: v = u + at and Delta r = ut + 0.5*a*t^2 independently along each orthogonal axis
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Adding vector magnitudes algebraically without resolving into orthogonal components

first_move_atlas.cue: Horizontal launch from cliff or tower with speed u and zero initial vertical velocity (u_y = 0)
first_move_atlas.representation: Origin at launch edge, +x horizontal, +y downward (or +y upward with launch at y = h)
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Solve vertical free-fall time first: t_fall = sqrt(2h / g), then determine horizontal range x = u * t_fall
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Believing higher horizontal launch velocity changes the vertical time of fall

first_move_atlas.cue: Oblique ground-to-ground projectile launch at elevation angle theta above horizontal
first_move_atlas.representation: Launch velocity decomposed into u_x = u cos theta and u_y = u sin theta; apex summit at v_y = 0
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Set vertical apex velocity v_y = u sin theta - gt = 0 => t_apex = (u sin theta) / g; total flight time T = (2u sin theta) / g
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Setting total velocity to zero at the apex (horizontal speed u_x = u cos theta remains strictly non-zero)

first_move_atlas.cue: Ground-to-ground horizontal range, maximum range, or landing impact coordinate
first_move_atlas.representation: Parabolic trajectory arc with landing coordinates (R, 0)
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Compute range R = u_x * T = (u^2 sin 2theta) / g; maximum range occurs at theta = 45 deg where R_max = u^2 / g
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Applying the level-ground range formula R = (u^2 sin 2theta)/g when launch and landing heights are unequal

first_move_atlas.cue: Two projectiles with equal launch speeds achieving identical horizontal range
first_move_atlas.representation: Dual trajectory arcs showing steep lob vs flat drive with complementary launch angles
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Apply complementary angle degeneracy: theta_1 + theta_2 = 90 deg => sin(2*theta_1) = sin(2*theta_2); ranges are identical, flight times scale as T1 / T2 = tan theta_1
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Assuming equal range implies equal flight times or equal maximum apex heights

first_move_atlas.cue: Trajectory profile curve, target clearance at (x, y), or path equation without time t
first_move_atlas.representation: Cartesian trajectory curve y(x) plotted on spatial (x, y) coordinate grid
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Substitute t = x / (u cos theta) into y(t) to form trajectory equation y = x tan theta - (g x^2) / (2 u^2 cos^2 theta) = x tan theta * (1 - x / R)
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Attempting multi-variable time quadratics when the Cartesian trajectory equation connects x and y directly

first_move_atlas.cue: Boat crossing river with stream current velocity v_r and engine speed v_b
first_move_atlas.representation: Vector velocity triangle: v_net = v_b/r + v_r across river width W
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: For shortest time, steer perpendicular to bank (theta = 90 deg, t_min = W / v_b); for zero drift (v_b > v_r), steer upstream at sin alpha = v_r / v_b
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Steering upstream when asked for shortest crossing time (shortest time strictly requires heading directly across)

first_move_atlas.cue: Rain falling vertically while observer moves horizontally, or aircraft in crosswind
first_move_atlas.representation: Relative velocity vector subtraction triangle: v_rain/man = v_rain - v_man
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Construct relative velocity vector v_rel = -v_rain j - v_man i; tilt umbrella into oncoming relative rain at tan theta = v_man / v_rain from vertical
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Tilting umbrella backward or along walking direction instead of into the oncoming relative rain vector

first_move_atlas.cue: Particle moving along circular path of radius R at uniform speed v or angular velocity omega
first_move_atlas.representation: Circular orbit with tangent velocity vector v and radially inward normal acceleration a_c
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Apply centripetal acceleration invariant: a_c = v^2 / R = omega^2 * R = 4*pi^2*R / T^2 directed strictly toward orbit center
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Claiming uniform circular motion has zero acceleration because scalar speed |v| is constant

first_move_atlas.cue: Particle moving along general curved path with changing speed
first_move_atlas.representation: Intrinsic Frenet-Serret coordinate frame: unit tangent u_t and unit inward normal u_n
first_move_atlas.first_executable_move: Decouple acceleration into tangential a_t = dv/dt (changes speed) and normal a_n = v^2 / rho (changes direction); total |a| = sqrt(a_t^2 + a_n^2)
first_move_atlas.anti_pattern: Conflating total acceleration with centripetal acceleration in non-uniform curvilinear motion

nodes.description: Mutually perpendicular spatial axes (x, y) with declared origin.
Resolving vector quantities into independent orthogonal components u_x = u cos theta, u_y = u sin theta.

nodes.term: Oblique Projectile Flight Landmarks (Apex, Time, Range)

cognitive_conflict_matrix.concept: Apex Velocity vs Total Velocity Invariance
cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: At the highest point of an oblique projectile flight, velocity is zero because the projectile stops rising.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Only the vertical velocity component vanishes (v_y = 0). The horizontal velocity remains completely unchanged at v_x = u cos theta. The speed at the apex is strictly u cos theta > 0, and acceleration is still -g downward.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Strobe photography of oblique projectile: at apex, particle continues gliding horizontally at constant horizontal spacing Delta x = (u cos theta) Delta t.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: A bullet fired horizontally at 500 m/s will take longer to hit the ground than a bullet dropped simultaneously from the same height.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Horizontal and vertical motions decouple completely. Both bullets experience identical vertical acceleration a_y = -g with identical initial vertical velocity u_y = 0, hitting the ground simultaneously at t = sqrt(2h/g).
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: A spring launcher simultaneously shoots one ball horizontally while dropping a second ball vertically from the same height; audio sensors record a single simultaneous ground impact click.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: Launching at a steeper angle always yields greater range because the projectile stays airborne longer.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Range is the product of horizontal speed and flight time: R = u_x * T. While steeper angles increase flight time, they reduce horizontal speed. Complementary angles (theta and 90 deg - theta) achieve identical horizontal range.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Launching water jets at 30 deg and 60 deg with identical nozzle pressure: both land at the exact same horizontal coordinate.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: To cross a river in the shortest possible time, the boat should steer angled slightly downstream to ride the current.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Crossing time depends strictly on the velocity component perpendicular to the riverbanks (v_y = v_b sin theta). The river current acts entirely parallel to the banks (v_x = v_r) and cannot assist or impede perpendicular progress. Maximum perpendicular speed requires steering directly across (theta = 90 deg).
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Two identical motorized boats: boat A steers directly across; boat B steers downstream. Boat A reaches the opposite bank first every time.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: If an object moves in a circle at constant speed, its acceleration is zero because speed is not changing.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: Acceleration is the time derivative of the velocity vector. Because the direction of velocity continuously changes, uniform circular motion requires a continuous inward centripetal acceleration a_c = v^2 / R.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Whirling a ball on a string: cutting the string releases the ball tangentially in a straight line, proving inward tension was continuously accelerating the ball.

cognitive_conflict_matrix.intuitive_misconception: When running forward into vertical rain, you should hold your umbrella vertically or tilted backward because rain comes from above.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.newtonian_scientific_truth: In the runner's reference frame, the ground and air rush backward, so rain acquires an apparent backward horizontal velocity component: v_rel = -v_runner i - v_rain j. The rain appears to strike from in front, requiring the umbrella to be tilted forward.
cognitive_conflict_matrix.decisive_experiment: Driving a car through vertical rain: rain streaks on the side windows slant diagonally backward from top to bottom.
